title.narrative: Support to the National TB and Leprosy Control Program in BANGLADESH

description.narrative: Contribute to SDG 3 ‘Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages’ through early case finding, correct management of TB, including MDR-TB, and leprosy and preventive therapy for latent TB infection in the project area is ensured by 2026 maintaining preventive and protective measures for COVID-19. Technical expertise in MDR/RR TB management is developed among the service providers throughout the country.

Contribute to SDG 3 ‘Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages’ through early case finding, correct management of TB, including MDR-TB, and leprosy and preventive therapy for latent TB infection in the project area is ensured by 2026 maintaining preventive and protective measures for COVID-19. Technical expertise in MDR/RR TB management is developed among the service providers throughout the country.

The target population is the total population of around 33 million in the 14 districts covered by DF Bangladesh. Specific target groups are the Leprosy and TB assumptive, and patients and their families. Another key population are the garment and other factory workers, mostly women and their children. As to leave no one behind, special attention will also be given to children, elderly people, people with COVID-19 negative testing while having respiratory symptoms, and the diabetic patients.

description.narrative: Result 1 : Management of leprosy will be improved through earlier diagnosis and more effective prevention of disabilities, despite the increasing rarity of the disease. Health care providers lose their skill for leprosy diagnosis as they do not often see leprosy patients and people with leprosy skin lesions only (in early stage) do not seek care as the lesion(s) do not hamper their daily activities. They seek care when there are already visible deformities or disabilities in performing daily activities.

title.narrative: R1 Indicator 1 : Grade 2 Disability (G2D) proportion among new leprosy cases

baseline.value: Proportion of new leprosy cases with G2D is 15% which indicates that there has been significant delay in leprosy diagnosis in the project area.

target.value: Early detection of leprosy cases will lead to decreased proportion (12%) of new leprosy cases with disability Gr. 2.
Early detection of leprosy cases will lead to further decrease to 10% in disability grade 2 proportion among new leprosy cases.

description.narrative: Result 3 : Efficient organization of TB case detection and management in the newly industrialised DF districts will reduce TB transmission among factory workers (mostly women). Rapid and growing urbanization and industrialization resulted in internal migration from rural to industrialized areas. Bad living (shared accommodation in small rooms) and working (inadequate space with lack in adequate ventilation) conditions facilitate in TB transmission among co-workers and family members.

baseline.value: A total of 871 TB cases were detected from about 200,000 workers in these industrial areas

target.value: With increased access to TB services by the target group, number of TB cases expected to increase to 1000 in year 3
With continued increased access to TB services by target group, number of TB cases expected to increase to 1200 in year 5
